subComponents.title: Senior Director, Simulation and Research Engineering
subComponents.caption: Nov 2021 - Mar 2023 · 1 yr 4 mos

description.text:
Responsible for overseeing Unreal Engine's Gameplay Frameworks, Audio, AI, Physics/Simulation, and Networking teams, and helping align team efforts with overall engine and company direction.

Helped steer and direct Epic Research's R&D efforts.  Advised and set direction for projects and research programs to ensure that the boundaries of technology were pushed, but also that the results could be practically productized into Epic's engine and game products.

Represented Epic leadership for Epic’s Seattle office, managing the studio, operations, and process development. Fed back process and feedback to other Epic offices. Hosted town halls and set office policies.  Mentored, advised, and helped with career development across multiple disciplines.

Worked closely with the architects and builders on three major office buildouts (8k – 48k sq ft), designing spaces that were functional, efficient, and comfortable to work in. Assisted with value engineering, branding, budgeting, and interior design of the spaces.

Responsible for overseeing Unreal Engine's Gameplay Frameworks, AI, Networking, and Audio engineering teams.  Mentored developers and non-developers in multiple disciplines, including several new leads and leads-of-leads.  Additionally, led a small engineering team on researching and developing a next-generation scripting language.

Led engineering efforts on the "Valley of the Ancient" technical demo for Unreal Engine 5, including scoping, design, implementation, and coordinating engine and content teams to ship day-and-date with the release of the UE5 Early Access build.

Responsible for overseeing Unreal Engine's Gameplay Frameworks, Blueprints, XR, and Audio engineering teams.  Led engineering efforts on the Oculus VR technical demo "Bullet Train" and the full-game "Robo Recall."

Helped guide development and advise partners and clients outside the gaming space on integrating Unreal Engine technology into their pipelines.

Advocated for the creation of the OpenXR standard for XR based on experience integrating and working with new hardware in Unreal Engine, and served as Chair of the standards committee.

Led and contributed to the development of the Unreal Engine's Blueprint visual scripting system and the engine's XR (virtual and augmented reality) architecture and integrations.

Lead engineer on various VR and AR demos and projects, including "Thief in the Shadows."

Improved several core systems of Unreal Engine, including UnrealScript, the core linker, and various frameworks.  Additionally, contributed to architecting and implementing several systems as one of the first engineers on UE4, working on frameworks and early Blueprints.

Worked closely with designers on a small unannounced project, creating gameplay systems,  iterating on new gameplay concepts, and implementing cooperative multiplayer. 

Shipped Gears of War 3 and Gears of War: Judgement.

Built early support between companies to create an Exploratory Group centered around creating an open standard for virtual and augmented reality applications, and served for nearly two years as the first chair of the Working Group developing the OpenXR spec.  Led and facilitated working group discussions and contributed to the technical design of the specification based on experience integrating various hardware platforms into the Unreal Engine.  The specification is now used and supported by the largest developers and manufacturers in the XR space today.

Worked on the America’s Army (2.7 - 3.0) game, a first-person multiplayer game commissioned by the U.S. Army and built on Unreal Engine 2.5 and 3.0.  Responsible for gameplay engineering and Unreal Engine modifications, and contributed extensively to many of the systems underlying the game.  Additionally, was responsible for final engineering push and release support for the titles.  Assisted with management and direction of remote contract engineering teams. 

Contributed design work towards America’s Army 3.0, including design documentation and review.
